messages:
maria_acme: Hey @alyssa_support / @sam_billing — our April invoice (INV-2025-003) shows $1,234.56 but the dashboard totals $1,234.48. Customer flagged the difference, seems like tax/rounding. Can you take a look?

billing-bot: Invoice processed: INV-2025-003 total: $1,234.56 tax: $98.76 (system)

alyssa_support: Thanks @maria_acme — looping in billing + finance. Can you attach the PDF or a screenshot?

maria_acme: PDF uploaded: https://acme.screens/INV-2025-003.png — screenshot shows line items and tax per request.

sam_billing: @alyssa_support looking. Quick q: is this customer on per-request metered billing? If so our current invoice pipeline formats each request as a 2-decimal line before aggregation, which can cause tiny diffs.

jordan_finance: FYI we historically format and round each line to 2 decimals for readability, then sum lines. That policy can create cent-level mismatches vs raw dashboard sums. Might be the cause of the $0.08.

kevin_eng: @sam_billing can you paste the raw usage rows for that invoice? I want to repro the sum vs invoice logic in a test.

sam_billing: here are sample rows (anonymized):
```sql
SELECT request_id, amount_cents, tax_cents FROM usage WHERE invoice_id='INV-2025-003' LIMIT 5;
-- rows: (r1, 12345, 987), (r2, 12346, 988), (r3, 12347, 989), ...
```
We currently compute line_total = round((amount_cents + tax_cents) / 100, 2) per request then sum line_total for invoice.

kevin_eng: Aha — per-request rounding to cents then summing vs summing raw cents then rounding once will differ. Need to pick a canonical policy (invoice-level rounding) and consider locale-specific rounding rules. Can you create a tiny repro?

sam_billing: Quick repro I ran locally: 
```python
rows = [12345, 12346, 12347]  # cents amounts (without tax for brevity)
per_line = [round(x/100, 2) for x in rows]
sum(per_line)  # -> 370.38
sum(rows)/100  # -> 370.37
```
So 1¢ diff here; with tax applied per-request and different rounding modes this can add up to more.

jordan_finance: Note: the client is EU-based and VAT (20%) is applied per request in our ledger before invoice formatting. Per-request VAT rounding increases the delta.

alyssa_support: Proposed immediate action: issue a small credit for the difference ($0.08) to make the invoice match the dashboard, and open an engineering ticket to change aggregation behavior. @jordan_finance ok to approve credit?

jordan_finance: Approving 8¢ credit. Please update invoice and send credit note/email to the customer.

sam_billing: I'll open an engineering ticket to change the pipeline to sum raw cents/tax for the invoice and only format/round at invoice-level, with a feature flag per-customer. Ticket created: BIL-472.

kevin_eng: I'll pick up BIL-472. Plan: (1) use integer-cent arithmetic everywhere, (2) sum totals at invoice level, (3) add country-specific rounding rules (banker's rounding where required), (4) unit tests + end-to-end test comparing dashboard vs invoice. Will also add a migration to recompute historical invoices if needed.

alyssa_support: Thanks everyone. @maria_acme we'll issue the credit and updated INV-2025-003 today and follow up once engineering ships the change. Apologies for the inconvenience :pray:

maria_acme: Thanks team — appreciate the quick response! :tada:
